title: Harden parsing with seeded mutation tests and libFuzzer
body:
Step 2.7 of the split plan: harden the new parsing against hostile input.

## What's here

**Seeded mutation tests** (`MutationTests`, in `Tests/GitDiffKitTests`). Each seed picks a window of whole files from the kernel, redis, or swift-argument-parser diff, or a corpus of the structures they lack (CRLF, `GIT binary patch`, combined diffs of two and three parents, a plain `diff -u` file, a commit preamble, quoted paths, a missing final newline), then one edit:

- byte noise: a byte replaced, 1–4 inserted, 1–8 deleted, the input cut short;
- structural edits, aimed at header and hunk lines half the time: lines duplicated, dropped, swapped, or copied elsewhere, a line repeated 60–70 times (across the 64-line header bound), a hunk count nudged, zeroed, doubled, or pushed past the 2⁴⁸ cap, an `@` run resized around the 64-parent cap, a `diff --git` line switched to `--cc`, `--combined`, `-u`, or bare `diff`, a line of diff syntax inserted (binary patch markers, combined hunk headers, rename, copy, mode, and index lines…), a line marker replaced, a `\r` added, a newline removed.

Odd seeds then pile 2–6 more edits on top.

Every mutation runs the event parser and all three collectors (`ChangedLines`, `DiffSummary`, `Diff`) whole, in 1-byte chunks, in irregular chunks (mostly 1–16 bytes), and under a small line cap (preferably at a CRLF line's length ± 1). The rules (`MutationCheck`):

- nothing traps;
- every result is the same for any chunking, with and without the cap;
- the collectors agree: the model replays as the events, and the summary and `ChangedLines` are what the model's files say;
- **the model renders back to itself** (added with the merge of 2.6, below): every clean window renders back to its own bytes, file by file, and every mutated or piled input that parses without damage renders to text that parses back to the same model, up to its first combined file;
- **damage stays local**: the files outside the edit's footprint come out exactly as in the clean parse — their events, `ChangedLines` entries, `DiffSummary` files and `Diff` files — and damage reports fall inside it. The footprint is the files holding a changed line; a whole-line insertion lands in the file before it; an edit that breaks a file's `diff ` line also touches the previous file, which that file's other lines can then join. A `diff ` line resets the parser, so the events after the next intact one must match exactly (checked under the line cap too, where the clean parse is damaged as well).

Seeds reproduce on any platform (own SplitMix64 and bounded draws, not the stdlib's `random(in:using:)`). A failure names its seed; `GIT_DIFF_PARSER_MUTATION_SEEDS` reruns one or a range (`'0..<100000'`, quoted in zsh), and `GIT_DIFF_PARSER_MUTATION_TRACE=1` prints each seed before it runs, for traps. CI runs 200 corpus seeds and 80 per real diff, about 4 s each in debug on macOS and Linux; arguments stay short (fixtures, not bytes). The windows' files are found with libc's `memmem`: corelibs Foundation's `Data.range(of:in:)` made indexing the kernel diff take 190 s on Linux.

Two bugs planted in the parser to check the checks were both caught with their seeds: a `diff ` line no longer ending a hunk, and a `\r` past the line cap counted as truncation (the second needed the cap aimed at line lengths, which it now is).

**Bug fixed: `ChangedLines.Collector` was quadratic on lines out of order.** Found by reasoning about the collectors' complexity, not by the mutations (they check correctness, not time). Each added line was inserted into a sorted range array, O(1) at the tail but shifting the whole array below it. 160,000 one-line hunks running backwards (4.2 MB) took 8.5 s in release against 0.02 s in order; 80,000 files of one path, each below the last (4.9 MB, a hostile `git log -p`), took 2.4 s, each doubling quadrupling the time. Now:

- a file's lines are kept as runs, sorted once at its end if they went backwards, and merged whenever they reach twice what the last merge left (at least 1,024), so memory stays a small multiple of the result (this last part came out of the review, below);
- a path seen again below its earlier lines is deferred and merged in one sort once it has as many new ranges as old (amortized O(n log n));
- `LineRangeSet.init(_:)` sorts and merges instead of inserting one by one; `formUnion` appends when it can, else sorts both.

Regression tests in `MalformedInputTests+LineOrder.swift` (the complexity guard fails on the old collector, 21 s; the memory test fails and the `Int.max` test traps without its fix) and `LineRangeSetTests`.

**libFuzzer on Linux CI** (`Fuzz/FuzzTarget.swift`, five seed inputs in `Fuzz/Corpus`, one step in `linux-tests`): a minute of coverage-guided fuzzing with ASan, trapping if chunking changes any collector's result. SwiftPM can't link a libFuzzer executable (it renames the entry point), so the step builds the library instrumented with `swift build --target GitDiffKit -Xswiftc -sanitize=fuzzer,address` and links the one file with `swiftc`; no new dependencies, nothing in `Package.swift`. Findings are uploaded as an artifact. macOS can't run it (no libFuzzer in Apple's toolchains); the file's header says how to run it in the `swift:6.2` container.

## Tests run

### After merging main (step 2.6, the round trip)

2.6 landed first (#7, `9dcb2ca`), so `origin/main` is merged in (`4715cc2`, no conflicts, no rebase). The checks record events through the shared `EventRecorder` and replay the model through `Diff.replayedEvents`, which 2.6 updated for `noNewlineAtEndOfFile(endsWithCarriageReturn:)`, `noNewlineAtEndOfInput()` and the new fields, so nothing needed adapting, and the fuzz target compares whole collector results.

`6726236` adds the round trip as a mutation property, cheap next to the chunked parses: a render and a parse of a ≤ 16 KiB window per mutation, and once per window for the clean bytes. The corpus's combined diffs move to its end so the rest of it is covered. The fuzz target renders every model and checks the same round trip. Damaged parses are left out by design, as `docs/diff-model.md` says, and the first seeds showed why:

- corpus seed 923: a `\ No newline` marker right after a `diff --git` line ends the header and is dropped as misplaced, so the `similarity`/`copy` lines after it rejoin the header on a second parse;
- seeds 60, 69, 92: a combined file's hunks aren't kept, yet they set its parent count and end its header.

A planted renderer bug (a marker's `\r` dropped) is caught at corpus seed 564.

- `swift test` with the network tests: 161 tests pass; `xcodebuild test`: 161 pass; SwiftLint: clean.
- `swift:6.2` container, `swift build --build-tests -Xswiftc -warnings-as-errors && swift test`: 161 pass (the mutation suite 10 s).
- Release mutation run, `GIT_DIFF_PARSER_MUTATION_SEEDS='0..<100000'` for the corpus and each real diff, at `6726236`: 400K mutations, clean.
- Fuzzing in `swift:6.2` at `6726236` (the target links with `-warnings-as-errors`): the CI step, 393K inputs in 61 s; then 5 min on 4 workers, 5.0M inputs, coverage 2,341 edges (1,792 before the renderer was in), no crash.
- `codex review --commit 6726236`: no findings.

### Before the merge

All at `014abbd` unless noted. New tests: `MutationTests` (3: the corpus is clean, corpus mutations, real-diff mutations), `MalformedInputTests+LineOrder` (backward hunks ×2, a repeated path's union, revisited lines stay merged, revisited lines' union, extreme line numbers, the complexity guard), `LineRangeSetTests.initNormalizes`; end to end, the mutation runs and the fuzzer below.

- `swift test` with the network tests (macOS 26, Swift 6.4): 141 tests pass.
- `xcodebuild test -scheme git-diff-parser -destination platform=macOS`: 141 pass.
- `swift:6.2` container, `swift build --build-tests -Xswiftc -warnings-as-errors && swift test`: 141 pass in 37 s.
- `swiftlint lint --quiet`: clean; `actionlint` on `ci.yml`: clean.
- **Long mutation runs** (release, 4 processes; each range runs for the corpus and for each of the three real diffs; odd seeds also pile edits):
  - `GIT_DIFF_PARSER_MUTATION_SEEDS='0..<600000'` at `d464920`, 2.4M mutations: 5 failures, all a harness artifact (piled edits made a line over 1 MiB, which the events cut at 1 MiB and the model keeps up to its own 64 MiB cap). Fixed in `3051366`; the 5 seeds pass.
  - `'0..<1000000'` at `16f9b11`, 4M mutations, 16 min: clean.
  - `'0..<200000'` at `1dc3c67` (after the review fixes), 800K mutations: clean.
- **Fuzzing** in `swift:6.2`: 15 min on 4 workers at `368c7db`, 13.7M inputs, a 1,312-unit corpus, no crash; the CI step as written, at `1dc3c67`: 520K inputs in 61 s, no crash.
- `ChangedLines` is `cmp`-identical to `main` (`693c8cc`) on the kernel, redis and swift-argument-parser diffs at chunks of 4 MiB, 1,021, 4,093, 65,537 and 1,048,577 bytes (swift-argument-parser also at 1 byte); redone after the review fix.
- **Kernel benchmark**, release, 4 MiB chunks, best of 5: main 0.087 s / 18 MB peak, branch 0.088 s / 17 MB (quiet machine, `ef0ea2e`); after the review fix, under load: 0.102 s vs 0.090 s, 17 MB both.
- **Hostile line orders**, release, 64 KiB chunks:

  | Input | main | branch |
  |---|---|---|
  | 160,000 backward hunks in one file, 4.2 MB | 8.5 s, 11 MB | 0.022 s, 24 MB |
  | 80,000 files of one path, each below the last, 4.9 MB | 2.4 s, 8 MB | 0.080 s, 15 MB |
  | one hunk repeated 1M times in one file, 17 MB | 0.084 s, 6 MB | 0.093 s, 6 MB |
  | 1M hunks alternating lines 1 and 3, 17 MB | 0.095 s, 6 MB | 0.098 s, 6 MB |

  The extra memory on the first two is sort buffers, bounded by the result's size.

## Review

`codex review --base main` (codex-cli 0.164.0): 2 findings, both P2, both real, both fixed in `6b7de7d`.

1. *Compact duplicate and overlapping runs during collection.* Runs out of order stayed pending until their file ended, so one file repeating a hunk grew memory with the input: 61 MB peak for 1M repeats (17 MB) against 6 MB on main. Fixed: they're merged whenever they reach twice what the last merge left; now 6 MB. Tests: `revisitedLinesStayMerged` (fails without the merge), `revisitedLinesUnion` (a `Set` oracle across merges).
2. *Guard adjacency arithmetic against `Int.max`.* `last.upperBound + 1` trapped on an added line numbered `Int.max` followed by another; the parser caps numbers, but the collector is public and hand-built events aren't capped. Fixed with the subtraction on the larger number. Test: `extremeLineNumbers` (traps without the fix).

Found in final verification, not by the review: the real-diff mutation test took 192 s on Linux (corelibs `Data.range`), fixed in `014abbd`.

After the merge, `codex review --commit 6726236` (the round-trip property and the fuzz target's rendering check, the only code beyond the merge): no findings.
